Their persistence paid off in the 39th minute when Eli Junior Kroupi latched onto a key pass from Marcus Tavernier to clinically finish with his right foot. The goal energized the home crowd, giving them a slight advantage heading into the break, while Manchester City faced the daunting task of dismantling a resolute defensive block. The atmosphere at Goodison Park was charged with anticipation as both sides locked horns in a pivotal Premier League encounter held on May 4, 2026. Establishing the tempo Manchester City controlled the early proceedings, moving the ball with purpose and probing for openings. Their persistence was rewarded in the 43rd minute when Jeremy Doku clinicaly converted a pass from Bernardo Silva , with Rayan Cherki providing the assist. This opener gave the visitors a deserved lead as they headed into the break, feeling comfortable despite the occasional defensive scramble. The Toffees strike back The second half transformed into a chaotic affair as the hosts surged forward with newfound confidence. Thierno Barry capitalized on a loose ball in the 68th minute to level the playing field. The momentum shifted entirely to the home side when Jake O'Brien powered home a header from a James Garner corner in the 73rd minute. The incredible turnaround continued at the 81st minute mark, with Thierno Barry once again in the right place to put the ball away, leaving the visitors stunned. A dramatic conclusion The visitors responded with urgency to salvage their campaign. Erling Haaland produced an excellent lob in the 83rd minute to narrow the gap. In the dying moments of the match, the pressure finally paid off: deep into stoppage time at the 90+7' mark, Jeremy Doku fired home a right-footed strike from outside the box following a Marc Guehi assist, capping off a spectacular match that ended in a dramatic 3-3 draw.

matches.description: Watch Manchester City vs Aston Villa highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 24, 2026. Manchester City and Aston Villa locked horns in a high-stakes Premier League clash that kept fans on the edge of their seats until the final whistle. The match featured a series of dramatic turns as both sides fought for dominance under the bright lights of the stadium. Semenyo Strikes Early for City On May 24, 2026 , Manchester City welcomed Aston Villa in a match that initially seemed to follow the champions' script. In front of a crowd of 60,332, the home side broke the deadlock in the 23rd minute. Following a corner sequence, Antoine Semenyo connected with a brilliant right-footed volley that flew into the back of the net. City remained largely in control for the remainder of the first half, heading into the break with a 1-0 lead and looking comfortable despite Villa’s organized defensive shape. Watkins Turns the Tide The complexion of the game changed almost immediately after the restart. In the 47th minute, a costly defensive blunder by John Stones gifted Ollie Watkins an open goal, and the striker made no mistake, tapping the ball home with his left foot. The goal was confirmed after a VAR review, signaling the start of a Villa resurgence. The visitors struck again in the 61st minute; Lamare Bogarde played a key pass to Ross Barkley , who set up Ollie Watkins for a clinical finish. Suddenly, the scoreline was flipped, and the visitors held a 2-1 lead. Late VAR Heartbreak at the Etihad As the clock ticked down, Manchester City threw everything at the opposition. Leon Bailey nearly ended the contest in the 76th minute, but his effort struck the post. The drama reached its peak in stoppage time when Phil Foden thought he had rescued a point for the hosts. However, after a lengthy VAR check in the 90+2nd minute, the goal was disallowed for offside. Despite a flurry of late chances and a blocked shot from Mateo Kovacic , Aston Villa held firm to secure a massive comeback victory on the road.
matches.title: Man City vs Aston Villa

matches.description: Watch Manchester City vs Brentford highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 9, 2026. The encounter between Manchester City and Brentford promised a fascinating tactical battle as two distinct styles of football clashed in the Premier League . With high stakes on the line, the atmosphere was electric as both sides looked to establish dominance from the opening whistle. A Frustrating Opening Half Played on May 9, 2026 , the match began with Manchester City asserting their usual dominance in possession. Bernardo Silva was central to their early efforts, delivering a series of corners that kept the Brentford defense under constant pressure. The hosts' first real chance came in the 26th minute when Erling Haaland rose highest to meet a cross, but his header was comfortably gathered by Caoimhin Kelleher . Brentford remained disciplined and searched for openings on the counter. Tension rose in the 22nd minute when the referee consulted VAR for a potential penalty to the visitors, but play was ultimately allowed to continue. The physical nature of the game became apparent as the half progressed, with Bernardo Silva picking up a yellow card in the 36th minute following a moment of frustration as the "Bees" held firm until the break. Tactical Shifts and the Breakthrough The second half saw Manchester City increase the tempo, leading to a pivotal double substitution in the 60th minute that saw Phil Foden and Omar Marmoush enter the fray. The tactical move paid immediate dividends as Jeremy Doku finally broke the deadlock, finding the net with a precise right-footed strike. Brentford pushed for an equalizer and had another VAR penalty check go against them in the 71st minute, leaving the visitors frustrated. As the game opened up, Erling Haaland took center stage. In the 75th minute, the Norwegian marksman found space in the box and clinically finished with his left foot to double the lead. The goal shifted the momentum entirely, allowing the hosts to control the rhythm while Brentford introduced Jordan Henderson to try and stabilize the midfield. Stoppage Time Flourish The closing stages were marred by rising tempers, resulting in yellow cards for Matheus Nunes and Jordan Henderson in the 88th minute following a flashpoint of violent conduct. However, the footballing quality remained high in stoppage time. In the 90+2 minute, Savinho and Haaland combined beautifully to set up Omar Marmoush , who finished from close range to put the result beyond doubt. With 59% possession and a clinical display in front of goal, Manchester City secured a deserved 3-0 victory. While Brentford showed resilience for large periods, the individual brilliance of the champions proved too much to handle in the final half-hour.
matches.title: Man City vs Brentford

matches.description: Watch Manchester City vs Crystal Palace highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 13, 2026. The Premier League clash on 2026-05-13 saw Manchester City host Crystal Palace in a fixture that promised tactical intrigue and high-stakes drama. Both sides took to the pitch with clear ambitions, setting the stage for a compelling narrative of dominance and resilience. Foden Orchestrates the Opening Act Manchester City established control from the outset, dictated by a staggering 72% possession rate. While Crystal Palace thought they had an early breakthrough in the 3rd minute, a VAR check kept the scores level. The home side responded with persistent pressure, as Marc Guehi and Abdukodir Khusanov tested the target from distance. The deadlock was finally broken in the 32nd minute when Phil Foden turned provider, setting up Antoine Semenyo for a composed right-footed finish. The pressure didn't subside, and Phil Foden once again showcased his vision just before the interval. In the 40th minute, he delivered his second assist of the match, finding Omar Marmoush , who clinicaly struck the ball into the net with his right foot. The visitors struggled to find a foothold, as offside calls and defensive organization frustrated the efforts of Brennan Johnson and Jean-Philippe Mateta . Late Drama and the Final Blow The second half saw tactical shifts from both managers, with Manchester City introducing Jeremy Doku and Nathan Ake to maintain their intensity. Crystal Palace sought a way back through substitutes like Daichi Kamada , but controversy struck in the 81st minute. Kamada went down in the box, but the referee ruled it a dive, booking the midfielder and extinguishing Palace's hopes for a penalty. Moments later, a defensive blunder by Gianluigi Donnarumma nearly handed the visitors a lifeline, but the danger was averted. Manchester City sealed the points in the 84th minute. Rayan Cherki , who had replaced Omar Marmoush , provided a brilliant assist for Savinho to sweep home with his left foot. In the dying embers of the match, John Stones produced a vital block against a shot from Kamada to preserve the clean sheet. After five minutes of added time and a final period of controlled possession, the referee brought a dominant performance to an end at the 90+7' mark.
matches.title: Man City vs Crystal Palace
